description: First-person adult guide demonstrating reading, writing and mathematics with real Bede replies and fictional Grade 3 role-play. Edited highlights; temporary access codes redacted. Natural chapter breaths are opened for reading; no spoken words are removed. Outcomes describe the intended practice, not measured gains.

segments.speaker: Guide
segments.text: I start with a book we've read together. Here, I'm using The Lion and the Mouse. I ask Bede to help my learner tell the story back in their own words. I listen for what they remember and how the events connect.

segments.speaker: Guide — typed request
segments.text: We've read The Lion and the Mouse. Guide a short Grade 3 lesson, one question at a time. Begin by asking me to retell it.

segments.speaker: Bede — recorded on-screen response
segments.text: Okay, let's start a bit smaller. What did the lion do first when he found the mouse?

segments.speaker: Fictional sample learner — typed
segments.text: The Lion caught the Mouse but let him go. Later, the Lion was trapped in a net. The Mouse chewed through the ropes and freed him.

segments.speaker: Bede — recorded on-screen response
segments.text: What do you think the story is trying to teach us about kindness or helping others, even if they seem small or unimportant?

segments.speaker: Guide
segments.text: For writing, I give Bede a short sentence to work on. My learner makes the change, then explains it. Here, changing help to helped makes the action fit the past. I can see both the revision and the reason.

segments.speaker: Guide — typed request
segments.text: Help me improve this sentence: The mouse help the lion. Ask me one short question at a time so I can make the change myself.

segments.speaker: Bede — recorded on-screen response
segments.text: Sure! Let’s look at the word "help" in the sentence. Does the sentence sound like it happened in the past, or is it something happening right now?

segments.speaker: Fictional sample learner — typed
segments.text: The mouse helped the lion. I changed help to helped because it happened in the past.

segments.speaker: Bede — recorded on-screen response
segments.text: Think about how we show that a verb happened in the past. Is adding -ed the only way to do that, or are there other ways verbs can show past action?

segments.speaker: Guide
segments.text: Now I'll try mathematics. I ask Bede to guide a problem about sharing twelve counters among three children. My learner explains the equal groups. I look for how they reached the answer, and whether they can check it.

segments.speaker: Guide — typed request
segments.text: I have 12 counters to share equally among 3 children. Help me work it out by asking one short question at a time.

segments.speaker: Bede — recorded on-screen response
segments.text: Great! Let's start by thinking about the groups. If you put the counters into 3 groups, how many counters would you put in the first group?

segments.speaker: Fictional sample learner — typed
segments.text: I put one counter in each group, then repeat. Each child gets 4 because 3 groups of 4 make 12.

segments.speaker: Bede — recorded on-screen response
segments.text: If you lined up the counters in each group side by side, how would you check to make sure all the groups have the same number? What would you look for?

segments.speaker: Guide
segments.text: I use these responses to decide what we practice next: remembering a story, writing clearly, or explaining a solution. Bring your own question and try Bede for twenty minutes.
